I couldn't run any of the baseline comparison: Bash refused every command that creates or writes a directory. I changed no source or test files.

## What was refused
Both attempts returned the same message: "Permission to use Bash has been denied because Claude Code is running in don't ask mode."
1. `mkdir -p /tmp/t5-baseline && git -C … archive HEAD | tar -x -C /tmp/t5-baseline`
2. `mkdir -p /tmp/claude-1000/…/scratchpad/t5-baseline` — the session's scratchpad dir, as the fallback you allowed.

Read-only commands (`pytest`, `ruff`, `mypy`) ran fine earlier in this session, so the block appears to apply to commands that write files or change repo state, including `git stash`, `mkdir` and `tar -x`. I didn't try to get around it with other write paths such as the `Write` tool or a Python one-liner, since that would sidestep the refusal.

## Status of work order 3
- **Not done:** all five steps (build the baseline copy, run the new tests against original code, diff the full-suite failure lists, clean up).
- **Nothing to clean up:** no `/tmp/t5-baseline` exists.

## Options to unblock
- **Run the setup yourself:** `! mkdir -p /tmp/t5-baseline && git -C ~/laguna-bench/runs/T5-A1/repo archive HEAD | tar -x -C /tmp/t5-baseline`, then `! cp ~/laguna-bench/runs/T5-A1/repo/tests/integration/test_update_concurrency.py /tmp/t5-baseline/tests/integration/`. I can then run the read-only `pytest` steps from there, if `cd /tmp/t5-baseline && PYTHONPATH=… pytest` is allowed.
- **Allow Bash writes:** switch the permission mode so `mkdir`, `tar`, `cp` and the `/tmp/t5-*.txt` redirects can run, and I'll do the whole order.
